rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” refers to the worldly punishment they tasted and the afterlife punishment prepared for them.
rows.anchor: اشارة إلى ما ذكر من الوبال الذي ذاقوه في الدنيا وما أعدلهم من العذاب في الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers came with clear proofs, meaning miracles.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات ﴾ بالمعجزات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They rejected the idea that human beings could be messengers, although they did not reject worshipping stones.
rows.anchor: أنكروا الرسالة للبشر ولم ينكروا العبادة للحجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They disbelieved the messengers and turned from faith; God has no need of creation or their faith and obedience, and is praiseworthy in His work.
rows.anchor: اطلق ليتناول كل شيء ومن حملته ايمانهم وطاعتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Protect yourselves by leaving sins and performing acts of obedience.
rows.anchor: بترك المعاصي وفعل الطاعات ﴿ وأهليكم ﴾ بان تأخذوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Require your families to do what you require of yourselves.
rows.anchor: بان تأخذوهم بما تأخذون به أنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This kind of fire is fueled only by people and stones, unlike other fires fueled by wood.
rows.anchor: نوعا من النار لا تتقد إلا بالناس والحجارة كما يتقد غيرها من النيران بالحطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase refers to the administration of the Fire and the tormenting of its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: بلى أمرها وتعذيب أهلها ﴿ ملائكة ﴾ يعني الزبانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers are the nineteen tormenting angels and their assistants.
rows.anchor: يعني الزبانية التسعة عشر واعوانهم ﴿ غلاظ شداد ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their bodies may be coarse and strong, or their speech coarse and their actions strong.
rows.anchor: في اجرامهم غلظة وشدة أو غلاظ الأقوال شداد الأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “لا يعصون الله” is a nominative adjective clause; “ما أمرهم” is accusative as a substitute, or means they do not disobey what God commands.
rows.anchor: في موضع الرفع على النعت ﴿ ما أمرهم ﴾ في محل النصب على البدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause means they accept and adhere to God's commands; the second says they carry them out without delay or sluggishness.
rows.anchor: إذ معنى الأولى انهم يتقبلون أوامره ويلتزمونها ومعنى الثانية أنهم يؤدون ما يؤمرون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is the alphabetic letter nūn; its sukūn indicates a disconnected letter rather than a common or proper noun.
rows.anchor: فالسكون دليل على أنه من حروف المعجم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets nūn as an inkwell; al-Nasafi objects that this noun would require inflection.
rows.anchor: قول الحسن أنه الدواة وقول ابن عباس أنه الحوت الذي عليه الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets nūn as the fish supporting the earth, named Tamhūt; al-Nasafi objects that this noun would require inflection.
rows.anchor: قول ابن عباس أنه الحوت الذي عليه الأرض واسمه تهموت فمشكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pen may be the one used to write on the Tablet, the angels' pen, or a pen used by people; God swears by it for its immeasurable benefits.
rows.anchor: أي ما كتب به اللوح أو قلم الملائكة أو الذي يكتب به الناس أقسم به لما فيه من المنافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “ما” may be a relative pronoun or a verbal noun; what is written may be the recording angels' records or records of good deeds.
rows.anchor: أي ما يسطره الحفظة أو ما يكتب به من الخير من كتب وما موصولة أو مصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing is God's favor to the Prophet, including prophethood and other gifts; the verse denies that he is mad.
rows.anchor: أي بانعامه عليك بالنبوة وغيرها فأنت اسم وما وخبرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “أنت” is the subject of “ما” and “بمجنون” its predicate; “بنعمة ربك” interrupts them as a circumstantial phrase attached to an omitted expression, with an accusative position governed by “بمجنون”.
rows.anchor: وبنعمة ربك اعتراض بين الاسم والخبر والباء في بنعمة ربك تتعلق بمحذوف ومحله النصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra bāʾ strengthens the negation and does not prevent “مجنون” from governing what precedes it.
rows.anchor: ولم تمنع الباء أن يعمل مجنون فيما قبله لأنها زائدة لتأكيد النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial answers the opponents' accusation that the recipient of the Reminder was mad.
rows.anchor: وهو جواب قولهم وقالوا يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر انك لمجنون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation identifies the Prophet's great character with God's instruction to pardon, command decency, and turn away from the ignorant.
rows.anchor: قيل هو ما أمره الله تعالى به في قوله خذ العفو وامر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says his character was the Qur'an, meaning its noble qualities.
rows.anchor: وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها كان خلقه القرآن أي ما فيه من مكارم الاخلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His character is called immense because he was generous with both worlds and relied on their Creator.
rows.anchor: وإنما استعظم خلقه لأنه جاد بالكونين وتوكل على خالقهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command urges firm resolve to oppose the deniers; they wanted God worshipped for a time and their idols for a time, while they spared him harm.
rows.anchor: تهيج للتصميم على معاصاتهم وقد أرادوا أن يعبد الله مدة وآلهتهم مدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers proposed alternating worship and protection from their attacks as terms for compromise.
rows.anchor: أن يعبد الله مدة وآلهتهم مدة ويكفوا عنه غوائلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They wished the Prophet would soften toward them so they would soften toward him.
rows.anchor: لو تلين لهم ﴿ فيدهنون ﴾ فيلينون لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is not subjunctive with an implied “أن” as a response to a wish; the construction instead reports that they already soften in hope he will compromise.
rows.anchor: ولم ينصب باضمار أن وهو جواب التمني لأنه عدل به إلى طريق آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporal phrase attaches to an omitted “فليأتوا” or “اذكر”.
rows.anchor: ناسب الظرف فليأتوا أو اذكر مضمرا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority take “uncovering the shin” as an idiom for the severity and hardship of the affair; no literal shin is uncovered.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أن الكشف عن الساق عبارة عن شدة الامر وصعوبة الخطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom evokes people baring their shins in hardship, as “his hand is shackled” can figuratively mean stinginess without any actual shackle.
rows.anchor: ولا كشف ثمة ولا ساق ولكن كنى به عن الشدة لانهم إذا ابتلوا بشدة كشفوا عن الساق

rows.speaker: المشبهة
rows.claim: Al-Nasafi rejects the anthropomorphists' literal reading as narrow-minded and deficient in rhetorical understanding; it would require a definite, familiar shin.
rows.anchor: وأما من شبه فلضيق عطنه وقلة نظر في علم البيان ولو كان الامر كما زعم المشبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are called to prostrate as a rebuke for abandoning prostration in worldly life, not as a legal obligation.
rows.anchor: لا نكليفا ولكن توبيخا على تركهم السجود في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot prostrate because their backs become like cattle's stiff legs and will not bend for bowing or rising.
rows.anchor: ذلك لأن ظهورهم تصير كصيا البقر لا تنثني عند الخفض والرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “خاشعة” is a circumstantial accusative referring to the pronoun in “يدعون”: they are summoned while their eyes are humbled.
rows.anchor: ذليلة حال من الضمير في يدعون ﴿ أبصارهم ﴾ أي يدعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disgrace overtakes and covers them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ترهقهم ذلة ﴾ يغشاهم صغار ﴿ وقد كانوا يدعون ﴾

words: وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود وهم سالمون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets called them to prostrate in worldly life while they were healthy, but they refused; that refusal is why they are barred later.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا ﴿ وهم سالمون ﴾ أي وهم اصحاء فلا يسجدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “الطاغية” can mean the event that exceeded the limit in severity.
rows.anchor: بالواقعة المجاوزة للحد في الشدة واختلف فيها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported view identifies the overwhelming event as an earthquake.
rows.anchor: واختلف فيها فقيل الرجفة وقيل الصيحة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported view identifies the overwhelming event as a blast.
rows.anchor: فقيل الرجفة وقيل الصيحة وقيل الطاغية مصدر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view takes “الطاغية” as a verbal noun meaning their transgression; al-Nasafi says this does not fit what follows.
rows.anchor: وقيل الطاغية مصدر كالعافية أي بطغيانهم ولكن هذا لا يطابق قوله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that he was supported by the east wind and Aad were destroyed by the west wind.
rows.anchor: لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم نصرت بالصبا واهلكت عاد بالدبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “صرصر” may mean intensely loud, from “الصرة” (a cry), or intensely cold, from “الصر”; repeated cold burns by its severity.
rows.anchor: شديدة الصوت من الصرة الصيحة أبو باردة من الصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind was either fiercely violent or beyond its keepers' control by God's permission, as wrath against His enemies.
rows.anchor: شديدة العصف أو عتت على خزانها فلم يضبطوها بإذن الله غضبا على أعدا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those before him” can mean the nations that preceded Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: ومن تقدمه من الأمم ومن قبله بصرى

rows.speaker: بصري
rows.claim: The Basran reading is taken to mean those with Pharaoh, namely his followers.
rows.anchor: ومن قبله بصرى وعلى أي ومن عنده من اتباعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The overturned cities are the towns of Lot, which were overturned upon their inhabitants.
rows.anchor: قرى قوم لوط فهي ائتفكت أي انقلبت بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “الخاطئة” means the wrongful deed or deeds marked by great error.
rows.anchor: بالفعلة أو بالأفعال ذات الخطأ العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who disobeyed their Lord's messenger were Lot's people, and the messenger was Lot.
rows.anchor: أي قوم لوط ﴿ رسول ربهم ﴾ لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were seized with exceptionally severe punishment, matching the increased ugliness of their offenses.
rows.anchor: شديدة زائدة في الشدة كما زادت قبائحهم في القبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Flood, the water rose fifteen cubits above the highest mountain in the world.
rows.anchor: ارتفع وقت الطوفان على أعلى جبل في الدنيا خمسة عشر ذراعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We carried you” addresses your ancestors, whom God carried in Noah's Ark.
rows.anchor: في سفينة نوح عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It” refers to the event of saving the believers and drowning the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: أي الفعلة وهي انجاء المؤمنين وإغراق الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event is a lesson and admonition for you.
rows.anchor: عبرة وعظة ﴿ وتعيها ﴾ وتحفظها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading with ḍamma on the dhāl is used by all except Nāfiʿ.
rows.anchor: بضم الذال غير نافع ﴿ واعية ﴾ حافظة لما تسمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A retentive ear preserves what it hears.
rows.anchor: ﴿ واعية ﴾ حافظة لما تسمع

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says it is an ear that understands from God and benefits from what it hears.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة وهي اذن عقلت عن الله وانتفعت بما سمعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He wishes he had not received his record because of the disgraceful things he sees in it.
rows.anchor: لما يرى فيها من الفضائح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealth he accumulated in worldly life did not benefit him; the object “anything” is omitted.
rows.anchor: أى لم ينفعنى ما جمعته فى الدنيا فما نفعى والمفعول محذوف اى شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “My authority” means his kingship and power over people; he is left poor and humiliated.
rows.anchor: ملكى وتسلطى على الناس وبقيت فقيرا ذليلا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the word means his proof: the argument he used in worldly life has failed.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما ضلت عنى حجتى أى بطلت حجتى التى كنت احتج بها فى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fetter him by bringing his hands together at his neck.
rows.anchor: أى اجمعوا يديه إلى عنقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Roast him in the Inferno” means put him into the greatest Fire.
rows.anchor: أى ادخلوه يعنى لا ثم تصلوه إلا الجحيم وهى النار العظمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “الجحيم” is accusative under an implied verb explained by “صلوه”.
rows.anchor: أو نصب الجحيم بفعل يفسره صلوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No close relative asks about another because each is occupied with himself.
rows.anchor: لا يسأل قريب عن قريب لاشتغاله بنفسه

rows.speaker: البزي والبرجمي
rows.claim: Al-Bazzī and al-Barjamī read the verb with ḍamma on the yāʾ: one relative is not asked about another or held accountable for the other's sin.
rows.anchor: وعن البزي والبرجمي بضم الياء أي لا يسأل قريب عن قريب أي لا يطالب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His clan means his closest relatives, who shelter him through kinship.
rows.anchor: وعشيرته الادنين ﴿ التي تؤويه ﴾ تضمه انتماء اليها

rows.speaker: يزيد
rows.claim: Yazid reads “تؤويه” without hamza.
rows.anchor: وبغير همز يزيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “كلا” rebukes the criminal's wish to ransom himself and warns that ransom cannot benefit him or save him from punishment.
rows.anchor: ردع للمجرم عن الودادة وتنبيه على أنه لا ينفعه الافتداء ولا ينجيه من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to the Fire indicated by “العذاب,” to the people as explained by its predicate, or be an implicit pronoun of the matter.
rows.anchor: إنا النار ودل ذكر العذاب عليها أو هو ضمير منهم ترجم عنه الخبر أو ضمير القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “لظى” is the proper name of the Fire.
rows.anchor: أو ضمير القصة ﴿ لظى ﴾ علم النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire calls sinners by name, destroys them, or their destination is described as calling them.
rows.anchor: من قولهم دعاك الله أي اهلكلك أو لما كان مصيره اليها جعلت كانها دعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those called are people who turned away from the truth and obedience.
rows.anchor: عن الحق ﴿ وتولى ﴾ عن الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is for Muhammad to tell his community what was revealed to him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قل ﴾ يا محمد لأمتك ﴿ أوحي إلي أنه ﴾ أي الأمر والشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority open the hamza of “أنه” because it is the subject of “أوحي”; “أن لو استقاموا” and “أن المساجد” coordinate with “أنه استمع”, while “أن قد أبلغوا” follows the transitive verb “يعلم”.
rows.anchor: أي الأمر والشأن أجمعوا على فتح أنه لأنه فاعل أوحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza is broken after a conditional fāʾ and after speech because the clause is an independent quotation.
rows.anchor: لأنه مبتدأ محكي بعد القول

rows.speaker: شامي وكوفي غير أبي بكر
rows.claim: Shami and Kufi readers other than Abu Bakr open the hamza in the clauses from “أنه تعالى جد ربنا” through “وأنا منا المسلمون”; others break it, connecting it to “إنا سمعنا” and pausing at verse ends.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في فتح الهمزة وكسرها من أنه تعالى جد ربنا إلى وأنا منا المسلمون ففتحها شامي وكوفي غير أبي بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A “نفر” is a group of between three and ten.
rows.anchor: جماعة من الثلاثة إلى العشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn were from Nasibin.
rows.anchor: ﴿ من الجن ﴾ جن نصيبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After hearing the Prophet recite during the dawn prayer, the jinn returned to their people and told them what they heard.
rows.anchor: لقومهم حين رجعوا اليهم من استماع قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في صلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They called the Qur'an wondrous and unprecedented in fine composition and sound meanings; “عجب” is a verbal noun used adjectivally.
rows.anchor: عجيبا بديعا مبانينا لسائر الكتب في حسن نظمه وصحة معانيه والعجب ما يكون خارجا عن العادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase belongs to the revelation, and the lām connects to “فلا تدعوا”.
rows.anchor: من جملة الموحى أن اللام متعلقة بلا تدعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not invoke anyone alongside God in mosques, which are devoted to God and His worship.
rows.anchor: في المساجد لأنها خالصة لله ولعبادته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes “mosques” to mean the body parts used in prostration: forehead, hands, knees, and feet.
rows.anchor: وقيل المساجد أعضاء السجود وهي الجبهة واليدان والركبتان والقدمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God's servant” is Muhammad as he rose to pray; the construction implies “وأوحي إلي أنه لما قام”.
rows.anchor: محمدعليه السلام إلى الصلاة وتقديره وأوحى إلى أنه لما قام عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He was worshipping God and reciting the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يدعوه ﴾ يعبده ويقرأ القرآن ولم يقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “servant of God” is dear to the Prophet; it also suits humility in his own speech, or signals that his worship is no surprise warranting a crowd.
rows.anchor: لأنه من أحب الاسماء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولأنه لما كان واقعا في كلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn nearly crowded around him in groups, marveling at his worship, imitating his companions, and admiring a recitation unlike anything they had seen.
rows.anchor: تعجبا مما رأوا من عبادته واقتداء أصحابه به واعجابا بما تلاه من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet says that he invokes his Lord alone and associates no one with Him in worship.
rows.anchor: وحده قال غير عاصم وحمزة ﴿ ولا أشرك به أحدا ﴾ في العبادة فلم تتعجبون

rows.speaker: غير عاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: The segment notes a reading difference involving readers other than ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah, but gives no distinct wording in this excerpt.
rows.anchor: وحده قال غير عاصم وحمزة ﴿ ولا أشرك به أحدا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement challenges the jinn's amazement and crowding around the Prophet as he worships God alone.
rows.anchor: فلم تتعجبون وتزدحمون على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, known among his people as “the one and only”.
rows.anchor: إلى عيني الوليد بن المغيرة وكان يلقب في قومه بالوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “ومن خلقت” may be coordinated with the preceding object or construed as a comitative object.
rows.anchor: ومن خلقت معطوف أو مفعول معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “وحيدا” may be circumstantial from the yāʾ in “ذرني”, the tāʾ in “خلقت”, a deleted pronoun, or “من”.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وحيدا ﴾ حال من الياء في ذرني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it describes the yāʾ in “ذرني”, God says to leave him alone with Me, for God will handle him.
rows.anchor: أي اترني وحدي معه فإني أكفيك أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it describes the tāʾ in “خلقت”, God created him alone without a partner, family, or wealth before blessing him.
rows.anchor: أي خلقته وحدي لم يشركني في خلقه أحدا ومن الهاء المحذوفة أو من أي خلقته منفردا بلا أهل ولا مال ثم انعمت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wealth was abundant or continually growing; it included crops, livestock, and trade.
rows.anchor: مبسوطا كثيرا أو ممدودا بالنماء وكان له الزرع والضرع والتجارة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports that al-Walid had one hundred thousand dinars.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد كان له مائة ألف دينار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also reports that he had land at Taif whose produce never ceased.
rows.anchor: وعنه أن له أرضا بالطائف لا ينقطع ثمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His ten sons were present with him in Mecca because they were wealthy enough not to travel for work; Khalid, Hisham, and Amara became Muslims.
rows.anchor: حضورا معه بمكة لغناهم عن السفر وكانوا عشرة أسلم منهم خالد وهشام وعمارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God broadened his status and leadership, completing worldly blessings of wealth and rank; their combination is perfection for worldly people.
rows.anchor: وبسطت له الجاه والرياسة فأتممت عليه نعمتي الجاه والمال واجتماعهما هو الكمال عند أهل الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording expresses disapproval and astonishment at his greed: he hopes for more wealth and children without gratitude.
rows.anchor: استبعاد واستنكار لطمعه وحرصه فيرجو أن أزيد في ماله وولده من غير شكر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says he hoped for entry to Paradise and wealth and children there, as in his boast that he would be given wealth and offspring.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن أن أزيد أن أدخله الجنة فاوتيه مالا وولدا كما قال لأوتين مالا وولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “كلا” cuts off his hope: after this he will not receive more blessings while persisting in disbelief; his wealth and status declined until he died.
rows.anchor: ردع له وقطع لرجائه أي لا يجمع له بعد اليوم بين الكفر والمزيد من النعم فلم يزل بعد نزول الآية في نقصان من المال والجاه حتى هلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His obstinate denial of God's signs explains the rebuke: an ingrate who rejects the Benefactor's signs does not deserve further increase.
rows.anchor: وهو تعليل الردع على وجه الاستئناف كان قائلا قال لما لا يزال فقيل إنه جحد آيات المنعم وكفر بذلك نعمته والمكافر لا يستحق المزيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I shall make him enter it” explains the earlier threat “سأرهقه سعودا”.
rows.anchor: سأدخله بدل من سأرهقه سعودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqar is the proper name of Hell and is diptote because it is a feminine proper noun.
rows.anchor: علم لجنهم ولم ينصرف للتعريف والتأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “لواحة” is the predicate of an omitted subject, “هي”.
rows.anchor: خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي هي لواحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “البشر” means skin; the Fire blackens and burns it.
rows.anchor: جمع بشرة وهي ظاهر الجلدي أي مسودة للجلود ومحرقة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers of the Fire are angels, unlike the punished; they show no pity and each has the strength of both humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: لانهم خلاف جنس المعذبين فلا تأخذهم الرأفة والرقة لأنهم أشد الخق بأسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers' number is nineteen.
rows.anchor: تسعة عشر ﴿ إلا فتنة ﴾ أي ابتلاء واختيارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jahl boasted that, being strong, he could handle seventeen keepers and challenged others to deal with two; the verse clarifies that the keepers are powerful angels, not men one can overcome.
rows.anchor: حتى قال أبو جهل لما نزلت وكان شديد البطش أنا أكفيكم سبعة عشر فاكفوني أنتم اثنين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation assigns six angels to lead unbelievers into the Fire, six to drive them, six to strike with iron maces, and Malik to guard Hell as their chief.
rows.anchor: ان ستة منهم يقودون الكفرة إلى النار وستة يسوقونهم وستة يضربونهم بمقامع الحديد والآخر خازن جهنم وهومالك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says Saqar has nineteen levels, each overseen by an angel.
rows.anchor: وقيل في سقر تسعة عشر دركا وقد سلط على كل درك ملك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation assigns an angel to each of nineteen kinds of torment in Hell.
rows.anchor: وقيل يعذب فيها بتسعة عشر لونا من العذاب وعلى كل لون ملك موكل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation compares the nineteen keepers to mountains securing the earth and says Hell's original number was one hundred ninety.
rows.anchor: وقيل ان جهنم تحفظ بما تحفظ به الأرض من الجبال وهي تسعة عشر وكان اصلها مائة وتسعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book know the keepers' number as nineteen from their scriptures, so hearing it in the Qur'an confirms its divine origin for them.
rows.anchor: لأن عدتهم تسعة عشر في الكتابين فاذا سمعوا بمثلها في القرآن أيقنوا أنه منزل من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers' faith increases because they affirm this as they affirm the rest of revelation, or gain certainty from the agreement with their scripture.
rows.anchor: لتصديقهم بذلك كما صدقوا سائر ما أنزل أو يزدادوا يقينا لموافقة كتابهم كتاب أولئك

words: ولا يرتاب الذين أوتوا الكتاب والمؤمنون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the People of the Book and believers do not doubt reiterates the certainty and increase of faith just mentioned.
rows.anchor: هذا عطف أيضا وفيه توكيد للاستيقان وزيادة الايمان إذ الاستيقان وازدياد الايمان دالان على انتفاء الارتياب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those with sickness in their hearts” can mean hypocrites; although hypocrisy arose in Medina, the verse predicts future hypocrites after the Hijra, while the disbelievers are in Mecca.
rows.anchor: نفاق ﴿ والكافرون ﴾ والمشركون فان قلت النفاق ظهر في المدينة والسورة مكية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the sickness as doubt, since most people of Mecca were doubtful.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالمرض الشك والارتياب لأن أهل مكة كن أكثرهم شاكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “مثلا” may be an accusative of specification or a circumstantial accusative from “هذا”.
rows.anchor: ومثلا تمييز لهذا أو حال منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strange number is called a parable because it would circulate like proverbs; doubters use it to deny revelation, arguing that a divine count would not be an incomplete nineteen.
rows.anchor: ولما كان ذكر العدد في غاية الغرابة وان مثله حقيق بان تسير به الركبان سيرها بالأمثال سمي مثلا

words: كذلك يضل الله من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God misguides those He knows choose error and guides those He knows choose guidance; the passage supports attributing the creation of acts and guidance and misguidance to God.
rows.anchor: مثل لتصديقه ورؤية الحكمة في ذلك يضل الله من يشاء من عباده وهو الذي علم منه اختيار الضلال

words: وما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Abu Jahl questioned whether Muhammad's Lord had only nineteen helpers, God says only He knows the innumerable hosts; He could easily make the keepers twenty, but their number has hidden wisdom.
rows.anchor: ولما قال أبو جهل لعنه الله اما لرب محمد اعوان إلا تسعة عشر نزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “هي” may refer to Saqar and its description, or to the verses describing it; the phrase means a reminder to humanity.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وما هي ﴾ متصل بوصف سقر وهي ضميرها أي وما سقر وصفتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they were not among those who prayed because they did not believe prayer was obligatory.
rows.anchor: أي لم نعتقد فرضيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “كلا” rebukes the demand to escape.
rows.anchor: ردع عن طلب المفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no refuge.
rows.anchor: ردع عن طلب المفر ﴿ لا وزر ﴾ لا ملجأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final destination is exclusively in the hands of the Lord: He wills whom to put in Paradise and whom in Hell.
rows.anchor: مستقر العباد أو موضع قرارهم من جنة أو نار مفوض ذلك لمشيئته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “المستقر” can mean the servants' settled state or the place they will settle, Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: مستقر العباد أو موضع قرارهم من جنة أو نار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet began reciting before Gabriel finished, fearing the revelation would slip from memory; he was told not to read along while Gabriel recites, so he could retain it without haste.
rows.anchor: وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم يأخذ في القراءة قبل فراغ جبريل كراهة أن يتفلت منه فقيل له لا تحرك لسانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will gather the Qur'an in the Prophet's breast and establish its recitation on his tongue.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن علينا جمعه ﴾ في صدرك ﴿ وقرآنه ﴾ واثبات قراءته في لسانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “قرآنه” means its recitation.
rows.anchor: والقرآن القراءة ونحوه ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى اليك وحيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When We recite it” means when Gabriel recites it to the Prophet; Gabriel's recitation is attributed to God.
rows.anchor: أي قرأه عليك جبريل فجعل قراءة جبريل قراءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should follow Gabriel's recitation as it is read to him.
rows.anchor: أي قراءته عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will explain the Qur'an if any of its meanings are unclear to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: إذا اشكل عليك شيء من معانيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “المساق” is a verbal noun from “ساقه”.
rows.anchor: هو مصدر ساقه أي مساق العباد إلى حيث أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servants are driven where God commands, either to Paradise or to Hell.
rows.anchor: مساق العباد إلى حيث أمر الله اما إلى الجنة أو إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He did not affirm the Messenger or the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: بالرسول والقرآن ﴿ ولا صلى ﴾ الإنسان في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human who did not pray is the one mentioned in “Does man think We will not assemble his bones?”.
rows.anchor: الإنسان في قوله أيحسب الإنسان ان لن يجمع عظامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He denied the Qur'an and turned away from faith.
rows.anchor: بالقرآن ﴿ وتولى ﴾ عن الإيمان أو فلا صدق ما له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative construes the phrase as withholding charity: he did not give zakat from his wealth.
rows.anchor: أو فلا صدق ما له يعني فلا زكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “يتمطى” means strutting; its original form is “يتمطط”, meaning to stretch, since a swaggerer lengthens his stride.
rows.anchor: يتبختر واصله يتمطط أي يتمدد لأن المتبختر يمد خطاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ changed to yāʾ to avoid three identical letters meeting.
rows.anchor: فابدات الطاء ياء لاجتماع ثلاثة أحرف متماثلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “أولى لك” means “woe to you” and curses him to meet what he hates.
rows.anchor: بمعنى ويل لك وهو دعاء عليه بأن يليه ما يكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After forty days the semen becomes a solid clot of blood; God then creates and forms a human being upright.
rows.anchor: بعد اربعين يوما ﴿ فخلق فسوى ﴾ فخلق الله منه بشرا سويا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Be patient in conveying the message, bearing harm, and waiting for victory over the Meccan enemies.
rows.anchor: عليك بتبليغ الرسالة واحتمال الأذية وتأخير نصرتك على أعدائك من أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not obey unbelievers out of frustration over delayed victory when they call you to sin or disbelief; obeying a request that is neither is not forbidden.
rows.anchor: من الكفرة للضجر من تأخير الظفر ﴿ إثما ﴾ راكبا لما هو آثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An “آثم” commits sin and invites the Prophet to it; a “كفور” commits disbelief and invites him to it.
rows.anchor: راكبا لما هو آثم داعيا لكل اليه ﴿ أو كفورا ﴾ فاعلا لما هو كفر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported identification calls the sinner ʿUtbah and the disbeliever al-Walid, respectively.
rows.anchor: وقيل الآثم عتبة لانه كان ركابا المآثم والفسوق والكفور الوليد لأنه كان غالبا في الكفر والجحود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is any sinner or disbeliever; “أو” forbids obeying either one, individually or together, whereas “و” might only forbid obeying both jointly.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد كل آثم وكافر أي لا تطع أحدهما وإذا نهى عن طاعة أحدهما لا بعينه فقد نهى عن طاعتهما معا ومتفرقا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes “أو” in the sense of “ولا”, so the instruction means do not obey a sinner or a disbeliever.
rows.anchor: وقيل أو بمعنى ولا أي ولا تطع آثما ولا كفورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pray the two evening prayers, Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ, during part of the night.
rows.anchor: وبعض الليل فصل صلاة العشاءين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perform tahajjud for a long portion of the night: two-thirds, half, or one-third.
rows.anchor: أى تهجد له طريق طويلة من الليل ثلثيه أو نصفه أو ثلثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “ماء مهين” means lowly, referring to semen.
rows.anchor: حقير وهو النطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It” refers to the water, which God placed in a secure repository: the womb.
rows.anchor: مكين مقر يتمكن فيه وهو الرحم ومحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water remains until a period known and decreed by God: nine months, or more or less.
rows.anchor: إلى مقدار من الوقت معلوم قد علمه الله وحكم به وهو تسعة أشهر أو ما فوقها أو ما دونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is a path all creatures cross: believers pass over it, while disbelievers enter it.
rows.anchor: طريقا عليه ممر الخلق فالمؤمن يمر عليها والكافر يدخلها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes it as a boundary where tyrants are watched for punishment, and as their destination.
rows.anchor: وقيل المرصاد الحد الذي يكون فيه الرصد أي هي حد الطاغين الذين يرصدون فيه للعذاب وهي مآبهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view says Hell watches for the people of Paradise, whom the angels receive there because they must cross it.
rows.anchor: أو هي مرصاد لأهل الجنة ترصدهم الملائكة الذين يستقبلونهم عندها لأن مجازهم عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transgressors are the disbelievers, for whom Hell is the place of return.
rows.anchor: للكافرين مرجعا
